title: What If We Built With Roman Concrete? Cracks Heal Themselves

scenes.text: What if modern buildings healed their own cracks, like 2,000-year-old Roman concrete?
The Pantheon's dome is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world.
MIT researchers found tiny white lumps in the mix, called lime clasts, once blamed on sloppy work.
Romans mixed with quicklime at high heat, which modern concrete does not use.
In tests, cracks in the Roman-style samples sealed in two weeks. The control never healed.
Cement makes about 8 percent of global greenhouse gas, so longer-lived concrete could cut that.
